correctness.rationale: Exact proof reconstructs Cesàro projector identity; for each n>=3 and g>=0, the two-point recurrence forces g²=1 if an eigenvalue is repeated. At g!=1 reflection gives rank<=ceil(n/2) and contains the antisymmetric subspace in the kernel. A nonwinding closed-walk count for 2k<n yields det W=(-1)^(q-1)(g²-1)^(q-1), giving rank>=q and exact kernel. At g=1 the independent published odd/even cycle projector formula supplies full rank/antipodal kernel as stated. All quantifiers, normalization, and n=3 and g=0 boundaries are covered. Exact rational and independent spectral calculations corroborate; finite tests do not prove the unlimited result.

originality.rationale: Direct primary full-text comparison does not find the all-order one-bond rank and kernel theorem. Godsil proves endpoint cycle and path formulas, which are explicitly credited, not reproduced as new. A general commutant identity or edge-perturbation characteristic polynomial does not, without a further exact nonwinding moment argument, imply the parameter-uniform rank, nullspace and unique transition weight. Searches of the available published results index found no equivalent statement; priority beyond accessible records is not certified.
residual_risks: An unlocated theorem on inverse spectral theory of cyclic Jacobi matrices, squared-eigenvector matrices, or generic reflection-symmetric quantum walks may imply the result; search coverage is not global certification.
Prior results for g=0 (path) and g=1 (unweighted cycle) were fully known; novelty is restricted to the uniform all-weight theorem and its exact moment witness, not those boundaries.
A broad computation theorem may enable recovery of this formula without publishing it explicitly; value and originality are judged for the explicit sharp characterization.

value.rationale: A single weak link is a canonical finite coherent-transport impurity. The exact rank jump for all odd cycle lengths is discontinuous at an arbitrarily small departure from a perfect link, while the even-cycle kernel changes to a physically distinct reflection contrast space at unchanged rank. The all-order determinant identifies the unique transition and gives a mathematical mechanism, not a small numerical gain or routine special case.
